title: From Counterfeit Detection to Sustainable Resilience: How Converged Digital Trust Technologies Secure and Future Proof Third Party Logistics Supply Chains
content: Counterfeit goods pose growing economic, security, and sustainability risks to global supply chains, yet research has largely examined blockchain, radio-frequency identification (RFID), and artificial intelligence (AI) as isolated technologies. This study conceptualises their joint adoption as Logistics Anti-Counterfeiting Digital Technology (LACD), a converged digital capability integrating identification, traceability, and analytical detection. Drawing on Rational Choice Theory and Deterrence Theory within a Technology–Organisation–Environment-informed perspective, the study examines the antecedents and organisational outcomes of LACD adoption, as well as the moderating role of government regulation, among third-party logistics (3PL) enterprises in China. Using 232 valid responses from medium and large 3PL enterprises and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), the findings show that perceived benefit, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty positively influence LACD adoption, whereas perceived complexity and cost negatively influence adoption; sanction celerity is non-significant. LACD adoption positively influences logistics security effectiveness and sustainable supply chain resilience, while logistics security effectiveness also positively influences resilience. Government regulation significantly moderates the effects of perceived benefit, perceived cost, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty, but not perceived complexity or sanction celerity. The study further proposes that LACD may provide an enabling traceability infrastructure for sustainable and circular supply chain practices. The findings advance organisational technology adoption research by integrating rational choice and deterrence logics, conceptualising anticounterfeiting technologies as a converged digital capability, and demonstrating the selective regulatory conditions shaping their adoption.
